text:
**For the safest bet, choose the Jackery HomePower 3000.** It has 3,000 Wh of capacity, and one estimate puts it at about **9.5 hours** for a queen blanket drawing roughly 260 W—enough for a night with a little margin. It’s a large, relatively expensive option, though: the cited list price is $1,499. ([runtime estimate and price](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/))

If your blanket is a lower-wattage throw or you’ll use a low setting, a **1,024 Wh power station** may be enough: the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is estimated to run a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, though actual runtime depends on how much the blanket cycles on and off. ([BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 estimate](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket))

Check the blanket’s label before buying: for a blanket that averages around **260 W**, the cited sizing guide recommends about **2,600 Wh** for eight hours; a 1,000 Wh unit would fall short. ([sizing guide](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/))
